QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_26

answer.text: An arrangement lacks commercial substance and its main purpose is tax benefit

explanation.text: The Logic: GAAR targets impermissible avoidance arrangements — those whose main purpose is to obtain a tax benefit and which fail one of the specified tests, including lack of commercial substance. Where invoked, GAAR can override tax-treaty provisions, denying the tax benefit sought. The Trap: Earning high returns, registering with SEBI, or making a commitment do not, by themselves, trigger GAAR; the trigger is the character of the arrangement, not the outcome or routine regulatory events. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook page 264, which describes GAAR's application to impermissible avoidance arrangements lacking commercial substance and its ability to override treaty benefits.
